A new road bridge over the Tumen River linking Russia and North Korea has opened to traffic.

Actual Article Body:
A new road bridge over the Tumen River linking Russia and North Korea has opened to traffic.

Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and North Korean Cabinet Premier Pak Thae Song took part remotely in the ceremony marking the bridge’s opening.

It is the first road bridge between Russia and North Korea; previously, the two countries were connected overland only by rail, across the Friendship Bridge.

The new bridge is just over 1 kilometer (0.6 miles) long, and construction began in late April 2025.

The bridge is named for Red Army officer Yakov Tikhonovich Novichenko, who saved North Korean leader Kim Il Sung from an assassination attempt in March 1946. Novichenko threw himself over a grenade hurled at Kim during a rally in Pyongyang, shielding him with his own body. He was severely wounded but survived, and North Korean authorities later awarded him the country’s highest state title, Hero of Labor.
